clue.text: Find love in a home on the water

indicators.note: love is placed in the middle of the word for a home, as the clue says

parts.note: a flat is a home, an apartment
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for romance while living on a houseboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O (love, zero in tennis) inside FLAT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floating rather than sinking is on the water's surface.

clue.text: Gets off with a slight fracture

indicators.note: a fracture breaks something apart, so the letters of the words a slight are broken and reset

explanation.surface: Someone escapes with only a minor broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'fracture' rearranges A SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to step down from a vehicle or horse, so it means dismounts.

clue.text: May be hung after views have been canvassed

definitions.text: May be hung after views have been canvassed

parts.words: May be hung after views have been canvassed
parts.note: reads like a political decision left in suspense after polling opinion; really a painting of scenery put on canvas and then hung on a wall

explanation.surface: A decision is left hanging after opinions are polled.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of countryside views is done on canvas and then hung in a gallery.

clue.text: It's accepted as a sin

parts.note: avarice is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A remark that some behaviour is tolerated though it is a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consented to by all parties has been settled and approved.

clue.text: Back a winner

definitions.meaning: to support or speak up for a cause

explanation.definitionFit: To support a cause is to champion it, and a title holder who won is a champion.

clue.text: Winter coat

parts.note: reads as a warm garment; really the white frost that coats the ground in cold weather

explanation.surface: A warm garment for the cold months.
explanation.definitionFit: A white frost forms a coating on grass and trees on cold winter mornings.

clue.text: Mild way to rebuke

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
to rate someone is an old word meaning to scold them

explanation.surface: A gentle method of telling someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. RATE meaning to scold is old-fashioned but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something temperate, not extreme, is gentle and restrained.

clue.text: People are clapped in these clubs

definitions.meaning: prisoners are clapped in fetters, shackles of metal

explanation.definitionFit: Shackles for prisoners are made of metal, and a set of golf clubs includes metal-headed ones by that name.

clue.text: Vengeance makes sin seem fatuous

indicators.note: fatuous means silly or foolish, so the letters of sin seem are muddled

explanation.surface: Revenge makes wrongdoing look pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so the word means just punishment.

clue.text: Disregard one note and not another

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
G is a musical note
nor means and not
E is another musical note

explanation.surface: Someone told to skip one musical note and leave out a second.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is to overlook it.

clue.text: Drawing-room lacking gin? Perhaps you'll find some here!

indicators.note: lacking means the clue word gin is taken out of the letters of the room's name
perhaps hints that the remaining letters are only one possible arrangement and should be reshuffled

parts.note: the letters of the word are used as written

explanation.surface: A sitting room has run out of gin, so the speaker suggests where to look for some.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove GIN from DRAWINGROOM to leave DRAWROOM, then 'Perhaps' rearranges it. 'some' means some gin: a wardroom is the officers' mess on a warship, famed for pink gin.
explanation.definitionFit: The officers' mess aboard a naval ship is where gin is traditionally served.

clue.text: Home shared by unmarried sisters

parts.note: reads like a house of spinster siblings; really a convent where nuns, sisters in religion, live

explanation.surface: Two spinster siblings live together in one house.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent houses nuns, who are called sisters and take vows of celibacy.

clue.text: Hercules initially joined Perseus going out to find wrecked ship

indicators.note: joined means the next piece is attached after the first one
initially takes just the opening letter of Hercules
going out suggests the letters of Perseus are dispersed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Two mythical heroes set out together to locate a lost vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' sits beside 'ship' as part of the definition: 'The Wreck of the Hesperus' is a famous Longfellow poem about a lost schooner.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's poem tells of a schooner lost in a storm, making it the best-known shipwreck in verse.

clue.text: Credit is twice provided in an emergency

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

indicators.note: twice means the word is should appear two times in a row

explanation.surface: A bank offers credit, doubled, when times are hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment of acute danger or difficulty is a critical turning point.

clue.text: Large vessel used as a pressure-cooker

definitions.meaning: a big ship powered by steam
a kitchen pan that cooks food in vapour

explanation.definitionFit: A steam-driven ship is one sense; a kitchen pot cooking with vapour is the other.

clue.text: Science article to copy electronically

parts.note: SC is a short form of science, as in BSc
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A scientific paper is to be digitised.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitising a document with a reader produces an electronic image of it.

clue.text: Laughing helplessly — even after surgery?

definitions.meaning: literally having sutures in a wound after an operation

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means helpless with laughter, and literally describes a wound sewn up with sutures.

clue.text: Bound to checkmate in game

parts.note: a bound is a leap or hop
to scotch is to thwart or put an end to, as checkmate does

explanation.surface: A chess player is certain to win the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', and 'checkmate' a chess move; 'to' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime involves hopping through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: First phase of Stone Age culture

indicators.note: culture suggests the words Stone Age are cultivated into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The earliest period of prehistoric civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The initial step of a project or process is its opening part.

clue.text: Food is dear, money needed

parts.note: dear and sweet both mean lovable
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Groceries cost a lot, so cash is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'needed' are links; 'dear' pretends to mean expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The thymus or pancreas of a calf or lamb is a delicacy eaten as offal.

clue.text: Without speaking, communicates a meaningful point

definitions.text: Without speaking, communicates a meaningful point

parts.words: Without speaking, communicates a meaningful point
parts.note: describes conveying something by gesture or sign instead of words

explanation.surface: Someone makes their point silently.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesturing or flashing lights conveys a message without words.

clue.text: Vegetable initially served before sweet

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
initially takes just the opening letter of served

parts.note: pud, short for pudding, is a dessert or sweet in Britain

explanation.surface: At dinner, a vegetable dish comes out ahead of dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is informally called by this slang name.

clue.text: Yet such timber may have been stripped

definitions.text: Yet such timber may have been stripped

parts.words: Yet such timber may have been stripped
parts.note: plays on clothed versus stripped: timber planed smooth is described as prepared yet has had its surface removed

explanation.surface: A paradox about wood that is both clothed and bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber planed and prepared for use is described this way, though planing strips its surface.

clue.text: Do in

definitions.meaning: a party or reception, as in a do at someone's house
not out, present in one's house

explanation.definitionFit: An informal reception held in a private house has this name, and being in means being present indoors.

clue.text: Where they will be good with a gear replacement?

definitions.text: Where they will be good with a gear replacement?

indicators.note: with attaches the abbreviation for good ahead of the rearranged letters
replacement suggests the letters of good and a gear are placed again in a new order

parts.note: the word is used as written

explanation.surface: A motorist asks where mechanics can swap out a gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges A GEAR as ARAGE after G; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Car repair workshops are where mechanics fit replacement parts like gears.

clue.text: Hood and sash worn in the Royal Navy

indicators.note: worn in places the garment inside the navy's abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy
an obi is a Japanese kimono sash

explanation.surface: Naval uniform includes a hood and a sash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like headgear but is the legendary outlaw's surname, defining his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw of Sherwood Forest is known by his first name and surname together.

clue.text: Magic Circle star?

parts.note: reads as a famous conjuror in the Magic Circle society; really a five-pointed star in a circle used in occult magic

explanation.surface: A top performer in the society of conjurors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a British society of stage magicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star symbol drawn within a circle is used as a talisman in occult rites.

clue.text: Record appearance of full moon

definitions.meaning: the round face of the moon when full

explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat round object, and the full moon looks like a flat round shape.

clue.text: First-class fare for Jupiter and Mars

definitions.text: First-class fare for Jupiter and Mars

parts.words: First-class fare for Jupiter and Mars
parts.note: reads like a premium travel ticket to planets; really the food eaten by gods such as Jupiter and Mars

explanation.surface: A premium ticket for a trip to two planets.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth the food of the immortal gods conferred immortality.

clue.text: Stout chap in Spanish parliament

definitions.meaning: Keats wrote of stout Cortez, the Spanish conquistador

explanation.walkthrough: Keats's sonnet 'On First Looking into Chapman's Homer' names 'stout Cortez'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conquistador Hernán Cortés is 'stout' in Keats, and the Spanish legislature shares the name.

clue.text: Fine words

definitions.meaning: a penalty imposed by a court

explanation.definitionFit: A judge's punishment, such as a fine, is one sense; a grammatical string of words is the other.

clue.text: Part of Hamlet's madness is dramatic technique

definitions.meaning: Polonius says of Hamlet: though this be madness, yet there is this in it
a school of acting built on Stanislavski's system

explanation.definitionFit: Polonius detects a system in Hamlet's madness, and the Stanislavski-based acting style bears the same name.
